title: Lawn trophies
hook: **WIP:** cosmetic **prestige** from lawn play — never stats, never a repeatable faucet. Not finished yet.

blindSpots.meaning: Not finished. You should not expect a full trophy case as a live grind yet.
Display prestige from lawn play. Not gear, not a soul sink, not a combat buff.
Design rule: trophies do not raise power.
Design rule: trophies are not a repeatable currency printer.
Your history of runs and progression — related memory, not the same as a trophy shelf. See [chronicle](chronicle).

alsoTrue: Blessing (soul boost on idle) and capture (roster intake) are different WIP lawn outcomes.
Play lawn for real faucets today — [souls](souls), XP, almanac — not for missing trophies.

sections.title: Not finished yet
paras: When it ships, earn trophies from play for display only.
Until then, treat a missing trophy shelf as unfinished work.

sections.title: Design guardrails
sections.intro: Why the page exists before the UI:

cards.name: Cosmetic
cards.body: Show what you did on the lawn.

cards.name: No power
cards.body: Never stats — prestige does not win fights.

cards.name: No faucet
cards.body: Never a repeatable currency printer disguised as medals.

sections.title: What you do today
paras: Chase shipped lawn outcomes: souls, levels, almanac meets, deploy.
Use [chronicle](chronicle) for history that already records runs.

doTitle: What you do while it is WIP
doSteps: Play lawn for souls and roster progress now.
When trophies appear, treat them as display — do not theorycraft power from them.
If a build ever ties power to trophies, that violates the design — flag it.

mixUps.q: Where do I equip trophies for damage?
mixUps.a: Nowhere. Design forbids stats on trophies.

mixUps.q: Can I farm trophies for souls?
mixUps.a: No. They must never be a repeatable faucet.

mixUps.q: Is this the same as blessing?
mixUps.a: No. Blessing is temporary idle soul pressure. Trophies are cosmetic.

mixUps.q: Why is there no trophy UI?

mixUps.a: Chronicle is history. Trophies are prestige display when they ship — related memory, different face.
